lines.1: 「...I understand now. You and Konoe had already made plans to hang out here.」
lines.2: 「Then there was no need to hide it in the first place.」
lines.4: 「What disappoints me most is that instinct of yours to cover things up.」
lines.5: 「Ahaha, sounds like he's getting quite a lecture downstairs.」
lines.7: 「While they're busy, time to snoop around Tsushima-kun's room! Here I go!」
lines.10: 「Don't rummage through his room without permission. That's just common sense.」
lines.11: 「What's the problem? I want to, so I will.」
lines.12: 「It's a problem. As long as I'm here, I won't let you do whatever you want.」
lines.13: 「My, my. You're like a guard dog. What a well-trained girlfriend.」
lines.25: 「Who said you could just grab my arm like that?」
lines.26: 「That's rich coming from someone who thinks she can just snoop through somebody else's house.」
lines.27: 「I do it because I want to. That's all.」
lines.29: 「I am the world, and the world is me. Too philosophical for you to follow?」
lines.32: 「No, it's fine, Sato-san. This is my chance to tell the Princess exactly what's what!」
lines.33: 「Heh... I like that look in your eyes. Your fighting spirit's burnin' -- burnin' with melanin.」
lines.34: 「You know, I love crushing people who dare challenge me like that.」
lines.35: 「Same here. I love tearing apart the arguments of conceited jerks and leaving them deflated.」
lines.36: 「Delightful. Very well--let's see you deflate me.」
lines.37: 「I've been itching for a chance to break that overblown pride of yours.」
lines.46: 「Fine. If I choose, I don't want you using that as an excuse after you lose.」
lines.47: 「And where does all that confidence come from?」
lines.49: 「Oh, Nao-chan. The drama club is accepting scripts for the play at the cultural festival, right?」
lines.50: 「Yes. We're set on staging an original play for the cultural festival, so we're accepting scripts as usual.」
lines.51: 「I could write it myself, but using a submitted work for the cultural festival is a drama-club tradition.」
lines.52: 「Though I can still submit an entry myself.」
lines.53: 「Right. Let's make it a scriptwriting contest.」
lines.54: 「You each bring a script you've written, then have third parties judge which one would make the more entertaining cultural-festival play.」
lines.55: 「Of course, we won't reveal who wrote which one. No personal bias--just a pure contest between scripts.」
lines.56: 「A script contest...? But that's my specialty.」
lines.57: 「That gives me way too much of an advantage.」
lines.58: 「That's fine. It makes for just the right handicap.」
lines.59: 「Besides, I write fiction now and then. Scriptwriting sounded interesting enough that I was already thinking of entering.」
lines.60: 「Oh? Then you're really fine with competing on that?」
lines.61: 「Of course. Which of us can write the script best suited to a Ryuumei Festival production--our cultural festival? Now that's an interesting contest.」
lines.63: 「Then we'll have 100 randomly selected Ryuumeikan students judge us! The contest will be on September 9, during the second term.」
lines.64: 「Let's make it an odd number: 101 judges.」
lines.65: 「Oh! You're right... A tie would be no fun.」
lines.66: 「I'll prove you're not good at everything!」
lines.67: 「And I shall show you exactly what an ordinary mortal you are.」
